instruments.name: YAMS Lab
instruments.description: Pedagogical demo of the Script (scr) module + YAMS. The voice (pulse osc → acid LP filter → amp/env → out) has NO LFO — every bit of movement comes from two Script modules. scr-1 'Rhythm Brain' is global/tempo-synced (arr lookup tables driven by `beat`, polyrhythm, `playing` mute) — press PLAY to hear it. scr-2 'Voice Motion' is per-voice/expressive (vibrato that fades in with note age + mod wheel, per-note random rate, velocity→resonance) — audible on any single note. Read the slot scripts via get_module_info(scr-1/scr-2).

modules.description: Pulse oscillator, the sole tone source. Pulse waveform is chosen so the pulse-width (pwm) CV input matters: scr-1 slot 2 sequences the width for a moving, hollow timbre. The fm input (exponential) receives scr-2 slot 1's vibrato. Frequency tracks the played note automatically.

Acid-model lowpass (TB-303-style ladder voicing) — the heart of the sound. cutoff_cv is driven by scr-1 slot 1's 8-step sequence (Env Amt 0.5 gives ~2-octave range); res_cv is driven by scr-2 slot 2 (velocity + random drift). Base cutoff sits low (350 Hz) so the script does the talking.

ADSR amplitude envelope → amp-1 cv. Also read back by scr-2 slot 1 via `src eg = env-1.out`, so the scripted vibrato tapers with the note's amplitude. Plucky acid settings: fast attack, 0.25 s decay, 0.65 sustain, 0.35 s release.
VCA. Its cv gain is shaped by env-1 (standard per-note volume envelope). No script touches this stage — the amplitude contour is plain ADSR, keeping the Script demo focused on filter/pitch/timbre.
Stereo output with soft limiter. Final stage of the voice; receives the amp output. Nothing scripted here.

Rhythm Brain (tempo-synced). out1 → filter cutoff (8-step glided sequence), out2 → osc pulse-width (5-step). Coprime lengths 8 vs 5 = 40-beat polyrhythm. Both gated by `playing`, so silent until the transport runs. Demonstrates arr tables, beat/modulo, lag, playing.

scripts.1:
# Slot 1 → flt.cutoff_cv
# An 8-step filter-cutoff sequencer. `beat` is the transport position, so the
# pattern advances one step per beat; `% len(cut)` wraps it every 8 beats.
# `lag` glides between steps (35 ms) so the filter sings instead of clicking.
# `* playing` mutes the sequence whenever the transport is stopped.
arr cut = [0.25, 0.55, 0.4, 0.95, 0.35, 0.7, 0.5, 0.85]

let step = cut[floor(beat) % len(cut)]
out = lag(step, 35ms) * playing
scripts.2:
# Slot 2 → osc.pwm
# A 5-step pulse-width sequence (bipolar, around the 0.5 base width). Length 5
# against slot 1's length 8 is coprime, so the combined groove only repeats
# every 40 beats — instant polyrhythm from two const tables, zero extra modules.
arr pw = [0, 0.6, -0.4, 0.3, -0.2]

out = pw[floor(beat) % len(pw)] * 0.4 * playing

modules.description: Voice Motion (per-voice, expressive). out1 → osc FM (vibrato: src-bound to env-1, fades in with age, depth from mod wheel, random rate per note). out2 → filter resonance (velocity base + rand_smooth drift, decorrelated per voice). Demonstrates src bindings, macros (velocity/mod_wheel/age), phasor, rand/rand_smooth, eager evaluation.

scripts.2:
# Slot 2 → flt.res_cv  (per-note timbre)
# Harder hits get more resonance (velocity), plus a slow random shimmer.
# rand_smooth re-seeds per voice from the voice index, so simultaneous notes in
# a chord drift independently — built-in movement/width with no LFO module.
let base = lerp(0.1, 0.6, velocity)
let drift = bipolar(rand_smooth(0.4)) * 0.15
out = clamp(base + drift, 0, 1)

song.name: YAMS Script Lab
song.author: Pertylizer Examples
song.description: A teaching example for the Script (scr) module and the YAMS control-script language. One acid voice with NO LFO module: all movement comes from two Script modules. scr-1 'Rhythm Brain' is tempo-synced/global (arr lookup tables indexed by `beat` → an 8-step filter sequence and a 5-step pulse-width sequence; coprime lengths = polyrhythm; gated by `playing`). scr-2 'Voice Motion' is per-voice/expressive (envelope-tapered vibrato that fades in with note age + mod wheel, random rate per note, velocity→resonance with rand_smooth drift). Press play to hear scr-1; preview a single note to hear scr-2. Open the scr modules' ƒx editors to read the scripts; get_yams_reference documents the language."

patterns.name: YAMS Lab Loop
patterns.description: 2-bar (8-beat) 16th-note acid bassline on an E-minor root (E2) with octave and 4th/5th leaps, accents on the downbeats. Length 8 = exactly one cycle of scr-1's 8-step cutoff sequence, so the filter groove repeats each loop while the 5-step pulse-width sequence drifts against it. Loop 0..8 keeps the transport `playing` flag true, which is what wakes scr-1.

tracks.name: YAMS Lab
tracks.description: Drives the YAMS Lab instrument. The only track in the project — the whole point is to hear the two Script modules animate a single voice.
